players.product: 8-inch and 12-inch wafer foundry and technology services (fabs in Shanghai, Beijing, Tianjin, Shenzhen)

quarterly_data.signal: First-half 2026 unaudited results (CFO Wu Junfeng): revenue US$5.511 billion, up 23.7% year-on-year; gross margin 22.9%, up 1.5 percentage points; profit from operations US$782 million; EBITDA US$3,545 million (64.3% margin); profit attributable to the company US$677 million. Co-CEO Zhao Haijun: Q2 growth came from both wafer shipments (+14.4% QoQ) and blended ASP (+5.7% QoQ); 12-inch wafer revenue rose 24% QoQ and 8-inch 11% QoQ; China revenue grew 22% QoQ on strong demand for AI peripheral chips, the return of overseas orders and continued localisation of manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue US$5.511 billion (+23.7% YoY); Q2 blended ASP +5.7% QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 EBITDA US$2,109 million, a 70.2% margin, up nearly 13 percentage points QoQ (CFO / Co-CEO); net cash from operating activities US$2,522 million and net cash used in investing activities US$2,271 million; H1 2026 capital expenditure totalled US$3.4 billion. CFO Wu Junfeng: Q2 EBITDA included one-time other income, and fair-value changes from associates and financial assets make Q3 EBITDA uncertain; excluding one-time items, EBITDA should stay high with utilisation and ASP holding.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 EBITDA US$2,109 million (70.2% margin); H1 2026 capex US$3.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 drivers (Co-CEO Zhao Haijun): the shipment increase was mainly driven by surging demand for peripheral chips brought by AI plus customer pull-ins - SMIC accelerated wafers close to shipment and slowed new wafer starts, and capacity built in prior years (about 16 months on average from tool move-in to customer release) came up to volume. SMIC allocated more capacity to tight segments, so AI peripheral chips, computer and tablet, and industrial and automotive revenue each grew about 40% QoQ; customer pull-ins lifted smartphone, consumer electronics and connectivity / IoT revenue 8%, 16% and 13%. Gross margin rose 5.2 points on higher blended ASP and better-than-expected utilisation, offsetting higher depreciation. SMIC plans to report AI peripheral chips as a separate application category next quarter or later.
quarterly_data.figure: AI peripheral, computer and tablet, industrial and automotive revenue about +40% QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 outlook beyond the revenue / margin guidance (Co-CEO Zhao Haijun): shipments expected to keep growing and prices to remain resilient; utilisation including newly added capacity expected to stay around 95%; the gross-margin rise is after offsetting incremental Q3 depreciation and peak summer power costs. Q2 shipments were largely wafers started in Q1 or Q4 2025 at old prices; SMIC prices from wafer start, so the new prices show more in Q3. Q3 will not repeat Q2's pull-ins, to keep the line running smoothly. Orders are already received into Q4 and year-end; he sees no possibility of price cuts this year ('at least maintained').
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 utilisation around 95% including new capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and supply (Co-CEO Zhao Haijun): SMIC added 8000 12-inch-equivalent wafers of monthly capacity in Q2 and adds capacity at a steady, even pace of a similar amount per quarter; it keeps 5% of capacity for R&D, so utilisation of about 95% is essentially the ceiling. Supply falls short of demand, also over the long term, in AI- and compute-related peripheral chips for data-center and compute boards - logic, BCD and optical-module transmit / receive chips. Overseas, some companies have stopped making specialty low-density memory and flash, and SMIC's capacity there is 'far from meeting demand', with prices rising. Customers of smartphone chips and display drivers (DDIC) for TVs and monitors can no longer get capacity and are negotiating future capacity and prices; customers' requests to reserve capacity have grown greatly since February, and SMIC is adjusting existing fab space to add more equipment.
quarterly_data.figure: 8000 12-inch-equivalent wafers/month added in Q2; 5% of capacity reserved for R&D

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing (Co-CEO Zhao Haijun): SMIC does not announce across-the-board increases but negotiates with customers; around February-March 2026 it agreed partial price increases in its tightest, supply-constrained segments, with no increases so far for smartphone chips or display drivers, where customers are struggling. He said that after the more than 4-point drag from higher depreciation, Q2 gross margin was about 9% to 10% higher than Q1 as the Q1-negotiated prices took effect; price increases contributed more to margin than product-mix optimisation (e.g., shifting logic capacity to MCU or specialty memory, and LCD-driver capacity to NAND flash), and new capacity is pre-ordered by customers and fully loaded at good prices. Further increases will follow supply tightness and are expected mainly in lower-priced consumer, smartphone and display-driver products, though not by a large amount this year. 'SMIC is never the first to raise prices, nor raises them the most.' Capacity allocation favours long-term strategic customers with prior commitments first.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 gross margin about 9% to 10% above Q1 before the depreciation drag (Co-CEO)

quarterly_data.signal: Depreciation (CFO Wu Junfeng / Co-CEO Zhao Haijun): 2026 depreciation is expected to rise about 30% year-on-year to close to US$5 billion (Zhao: about US$4.9-5.0 billion for the year), increasing by roughly US$120-140 million each quarter and weighing about 4% to 5% on gross margin per quarter; H1 depreciation was about US$2.3 billion. Under previously announced expansion plans depreciation would peak in 2027, but expansion plans are being adjusted to customer orders, and depreciation is expected to rise further after 2027, so the peak timing is uncertain. Zhao: SMIC will keep protecting its gross margin while expanding.

AI demand for mature nodes (Co-CEO Zhao Haijun): AI first drives the two ends - standard logic for compute and very mature analog, where 8-inch demand growth 'far exceeds imagination' - while 40nm / 28nm is pulled along only by spillover. Power supply and power management demand is very large: in a rack with 72 GPUs plus other components, power supply / power management parts alone can exceed 16,000. BCD demand and prices remain firm and supply-short, with demand visible to the end of next year; 48V high-voltage, high-current parts (needing 80-100V withstand) are mainly on 8-inch, while some single high-volume parts are moving to 12-inch. Smartphone inventory 'should be gradually getting high' after pull-ins, and customers in consumer and panel drivers are starting to stock up for next year, fearing capacity shortages and higher supply-chain, packaging-test and materials costs.
quarterly_data.figure: power supply / power management parts can exceed 16,000 per 72-GPU rack (Co-CEO)
